About Loan Against Mutual Funds Customer question Simple answer What is a Loan Against Mutual Funds? It is a loan given against eligible mutual fund units. Your selected units are pledged as security for the loan. Do I need to sell my mutual funds to take this loan? No. You do not need to sell the eligible units. The selected units are pledged as security. Will the mutual funds remain in my name? Yes. The mutual fund units remain in your name, but a lien is placed on the pledged units until it is removed. Can the value of my mutual funds change after pledging? Yes. Mutual fund values can go up or down with the market. The value is not guaranteed. Can I continue to receive gains or dividends on pledged units? Yes. Since your units stay invested, you can still get dividends or growth, depending on what that particular mutual fund scheme offers. What is a lien? A lien is a hold placed on the selected mutual fund units because they are being used as security for the loan. What is MF Central? No. It is a secured loan because eligible mutual fund units are pledged as security. What can I use the loan amount for? Are all mutual funds eligible? No. Only the mutual funds and units that meet the lender’s rules will be shown as eligible. Why are some of my mutual funds not eligible?
